intro: Protects buyers of goods and services — online or offline — against defective products, poor service, unfair practices and misleading ads. Complaints go to consumer commissions, which are cheaper and faster than civil courts. Helpline: 1915.

sections.p: Anyone who buys goods or hires services for payment (paid, promised or in instalments), including online, teleshopping and direct selling. Not someone who buys for resale or for a commercial purpose (except to earn a livelihood through self-employment).

Six rights: safety against hazardous goods; information about quality, quantity, price and standards; access to a variety of goods at competitive prices; to be heard; to seek redressal; and consumer awareness.
Any fault, shortcoming or inadequacy in quality or manner of service, including negligence or deliberately withholding relevant information.

Includes false claims about goods/services, misleading ads, not issuing a bill, refusing to take back defective goods or refund within the stated period (or 30 days), and disclosing a consumer's personal information without legal need.

Based on the value paid for goods or services: District Commission up to ₹50 lakh; State Commission ₹50 lakh–₹2 crore; National Commission above ₹2 crore (Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction) Rules, 2021).

You can file where you live or work — not just where the seller is. Complaints can be filed online through the government's e-filing portal. No court fee for claims up to ₹5 lakh. You can argue the case yourself without a lawyer.
The commission can refer the dispute to mediation if both sides agree.
Commissions should decide within 3 months of notice to the opposite party, or 5 months if testing of goods is needed.
Replacement, repair, refund, compensation for loss or injury, punitive damages, discontinuing unfair practices, withdrawal of hazardous goods, and corrective advertising.
Appeal against a District Commission order to the State Commission within 45 days; the appellant must deposit 50% of the amount awarded.
A complaint must be filed within 2 years of the cause of action. Delay can be condoned for sufficient cause.
Manufacturers, service providers and sellers are liable for harm caused by defective products or deficient services — e.g. manufacturing or design defects, or inadequate warnings and instructions.
The CCPA can investigate, order recalls and refunds, and penalise misleading ads. Celebrities endorsing misleading ads can be fined and banned from endorsements for up to 1–3 years.
Manufacturers or service providers who make false or misleading ads harmful to consumers are punishable.
sections.pen: Up to 2 years + ₹10 lakh; repeat up to 5 years + ₹50 lakh

sections.p: Failing to comply with an order of a consumer commission.
